key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings on Grade 2 titanium achieved the best tribological performance at O2/C2H2 ratios of 3.0–3.3, balancing phase composition, crystallinity, and adhesion.
engineering_relevance: These biocoatings can improve wear resistance and surface bioactivity of titanium implants, supporting longer service life and faster osseointegration in physiological environments.
method: Deposited hydroxyapatite on commercially pure Grade 2 titanium by detonation spraying.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio from 2.6 to 3.7 to tune coating structure and properties.
Evaluated phase composition, surface morphology, hydrophobicity, and tribological behavior in dry and Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: XRD showed hydroxyapatite as the dominant phase with some α-tricalcium phosphate, and tribology testing found the lowest wear volume and best friction behavior at O2/C2H2 = 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: Detonation spraying at high thermal/dynamic loads can induce phase changes and structural heterogeneity, so process control is critical to avoid inconsistent coating quality.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
